provenance.note: Assessment per mandal inside Visakhapatnam district, for the three editions on today's eleven units (2023-2024 to 2025-2026). Drilled below the district because IN-GRES classes Visakhapatnam district safe in all three (43.85% in 2024-2025) while one mandal inside it, Visakhapatnam Rural, was critical in 2024-2025 (95.06%). This is NOT depth-to-water - IN-GRES does not carry it; measured levels are a separate series from APWRIMS and the AP Ground Water Department.

source: IN-GRES - India Ground Water Resource Estimation System (CGWB + State groundwater departments)
unit_note: ham = hectare-metres. development_pct is IN-GRES's stage of extraction: annual extraction as a percentage of the annual extractable resource.

blocks.name: Anandapuram
blocks.history_caveat: The editions shown start at 2023-2024, the first in which all eleven current mandals are assessed: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one GVMC unit and Bheemunipatnam had other boundaries. The 2025-2026 IN-GRES edition is newer than CGWB's December 2025 report, and its rainfall input repeats 2024-2025.

blocks.name: Gajuwaka
blocks.history_caveat: The editions shown start at 2023-2024, the first in which all eleven current mandals are assessed: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one GVMC unit and Bheemunipatnam had other boundaries. The 2025-2026 IN-GRES edition is newer than CGWB's December 2025 report, and its rainfall input repeats 2024-2025. In 2025-2026 its estimated industrial draft is revised from 5.4 to 97.0 ham and its surface-irrigation recharge is cut from 111.95 to 19.19 ham, which together take it from 60.47% to 89.39% (semi critical); these are revised inputs, not measured change.

blocks.name: Maharanipeta
blocks.history_caveat: The editions shown start at 2023-2024, the first in which all eleven current mandals are assessed: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one GVMC unit and Bheemunipatnam had other boundaries. The 2025-2026 IN-GRES edition is newer than CGWB's December 2025 report, and its rainfall input repeats 2024-2025. In 2025-2026 its surface-irrigation recharge is revised from 171.18 to 561.40 ham and its extractable resource from 1,058.35 to 1,411.17 ham, while extraction stays near 720 ham, so the move from 67.26% to 51.34% comes from a revised input, not measured change. blocks.name: Mulagada
blocks.history_caveat: The editions shown start at 2023-2024, the first in which all eleven current mandals are assessed: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one GVMC unit and Bheemunipatnam had other boundaries. The 2025-2026 IN-GRES edition is newer than CGWB's December 2025 report, and its rainfall input repeats 2024-2025. Most of the area IN-GRES calls Mulagada lies in the mandal the AP Water Resources Department's map calls Pedagantyada, around Devada and Palavalasa, so the wells here carry that name. CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan for the Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli urban areas gives Pedagantyada 100 km2 and Mulagada 30 km2, against the 98.8 km2 IN-GRES assesses here, so the two names look transposed.

blocks.name: Visakhapatnam Rural
blocks.history_caveat: The editions shown start at 2023-2024, the first in which all eleven current mandals are assessed: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one GVMC unit and Bheemunipatnam had other boundaries. The 2025-2026 IN-GRES edition is newer than CGWB's December 2025 report, and its rainfall input repeats 2024-2025. In 2025-2026 its extractable resource is revised from 225.3 to 437.1 ham, with 223.88 ham of surface-irrigation recharge where 2024-2025 had none, while extraction stays near 210 ham, so the move from 95.06% (critical in CGWB's 2025 report) to 47.87% comes from a revised input, not measured change. IN-GRES assesses this unit over 39.0 km2; the AP Water Resources Department's mandal map gives Visakhapatnam (Rural) 130.9 km2.

notes: VISAKHAPATNAM RURAL IS THE MANDAL TO WATCH. In 2024-2025, the edition CGWB printed in 'Dynamic Ground Water Resources of Andhra Pradesh State 2025' (December 2025; district table PDF p.95, mandal table pp.108-109), it extracted 214.2 of its 225.3 ham extractable resource, 95.06%, and was the district's only CRITICAL unit, while Visakhapatnam district as a whole stood at 43.85%, which IN-GRES classes safe. This artifact reproduces that edition's eleven mandal figures to one decimal.

2025-2026 IS THE EDITION THE MAP COLOURS, AND IT IS NEWER THAN CGWB'S DECEMBER 2025 REPORT, which carries 2024-2025. It is the newest edition on IN-GRES, and every mandal's rainfall input repeats its 2024-2025 figure. Its surface-irrigation recharge differs from 2024-2025 in every mandal, and four urban mandals move by more than 15 points, all on revised inputs rather than measured change: Visakhapatnam Rural's extractable resource nearly doubles (225.3 to 437.1 ham, with 223.88 ham of surface-irrigation recharge where 2024-2025 had none) while its extraction slips from 214.2 to 209.2 ham, taking it from 95.06% critical to 47.87% safe; Gajuwaka's estimated industrial draft goes from 5.4 to 97.0 ham while its surface-irrigation recharge is cut from 111.95 to 19.19 ham (extractable resource 605.3 to 519.4 ham), taking it from 60.47% to 89.39% and semi critical; Maharanipeta's surface-irrigation recharge rises from 171.18 to 561.40 ham (extractable resource 1,058.35 to 1,411.17 ham), taking it from 67.26% to 51.34%; and Seethammadhara's falls from 103.69 to 53.36 ham (extractable resource 205.65 to 156.98 ham), taking it from 49.78% to 66.40%. Each moved unit's panel carries its own caveat.

EDITIONS START AT 2023-2024, the first with today's eleven units. IN-GRES also publishes 2016-2017, 2019-2020, 2021-2022 and 2022-2023 under the same district id, but on different units: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one 'GVMC' unit of 513.8 km2, which became seven urban mandals (430.2 km2 together) in 2023-2024, and Bheemunipatnam was redrawn from 93.8 to 124.2 to 207.9 km2 (Pendurthi and Anandapuram also changed). A series joined across those redraws would show jumps that are boundary changes. For the record, the single GVMC unit stood at 50.84% (2019-2020), 47.70% (2021-2022) and 56.78% (2022-2023), all safe.

ONE DISTRICT ID, TWO DISTRICTS. Andhra Pradesh divided Visakhapatnam district in April 2022 and IN-GRES kept one id across the change: its district rows cover 8,547.7 km2 in 2016-2017 and 11,050.6 km2 in 2019-2020, then 1,001.7 km2 from 2021-2022, the assessed area of the new district (CGWB's 2025 report gives its geographical area as 1,049 km2). The district figure goes from 27.22% to 45.96% across that change, which is the boundary, not the aquifer. No district series is published here, and no district trend should be quoted across 2021.

IN THE CITY, GROUNDWATER IS DRAWN FOR HOMES. In 2024-2025, 1,676.9 of the 1,776.2 ham extracted across the seven urban mandals (94.4%, summed before rounding) was for domestic use, while in Anandapuram, Padmanabham and Pendurthi more than 95% of extraction is irrigation.
No unit in these three editions is categorised on the salinity axis and none carries poor-quality area, so every figure covers the unit's whole assessed area.

THE MAP OUTLINES ARE APPROXIMATE. They are IN-GRES's own unit polygons (GeoServer layer gec:indgec_mandal_all, 2023 vintage, identical to the active 2025 vintage), but their areas do not equal the areas the assessment was computed over: together they cover 973.8 km2 against 1,001.7 km2 assessed, and Pendurthi's polygon is 77.2 km2 against 21.6 km2 assessed. The colours carry each unit's assessed figures; the outlines only place them.

IN-GRES'S URBAN UNITS DO NOT FOLLOW ANDHRA PRADESH'S MANDAL LINES. The unit IN-GRES calls Mulagada (assessed over 98.8 km2) lies mostly inside the mandal that the AP Water Resources Department's own boundary map (APWRIMS GeoServer layer AP_MANDAL_V3) calls Pedagantyada, around Devada and Palavalasa. The unit it calls Peddagantyada (15.3 km2) is a strip around Gollalapalem and Gopalapatnam. CGWB's 2025 aquifer management plan for the Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli urban agglomerations (Table 1.1) gives Pedagantyada 100 km2 and Mulagada 30 km2, so the two names look transposed. The other urban units differ in extent too: IN-GRES assesses Maharanipeta over 123.0 km2 and Visakhapatnam Rural over 39.0 km2, where the AP map has 45.7 and 130.9 km2. Figures are shown under IN-GRES's names. Each well's panel and label on the groundwater map name the AP mandal its coordinates fall in and, where it differs, the IN-GRES unit; the Mulagada and Peddagantyada panels say the names look transposed.

availability_ham IS THE EXTRACTABLE RESOURCE (the API's currentAvailabilityForAllPurposes). For Andhra Pradesh the API's totalGWAvailability adds the in-storage resource below the zone of water-level fluctuation, which is why Gopalapatnam would otherwise read 72,849.2 ham against an extractable 383.5 ham in 2024-2025.
